blocks.text: The hidden cost of account executive stress

Stress in sales roles is not just a personal feeling. It has a real price tag. Research shows that burnout costs companies between 4,000 and 21,000 dollars per employee every year. Much of this cost comes from presenteeism. You show up to your desk, but you are not working at full capacity. For executives, this hit is even larger, averaging 20,683 dollars annually. When you feel overwhelmed, your decision-making slows down. You lose hours every week just trying to keep up with your inbox and CRM updates.

The primary cause of stress is the gap between what you need to do and the resources you have. You are expected to hit high revenue targets while spending 31 to 40 percent of your week on admin tasks. This constant task switching forces your brain to work harder than it should. You might be in Gmail, then move to Slack, then jump into a spreadsheet. Each switch creates a small mental tax. Over a week, this adds up to 3 to 5 hours of lost time. The feeling of losing control over your own day is a major driver of burnout.
Fixes you can use right now

items: Define clear daily metrics to reduce uncertainty. Know exactly what success looks like for your day.
Practice box breathing during high-pressure moments. Inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 4, exhale for 4, hold for 4.
Take a walk during lunch. Even a short break away from your screen lowers your cortisol levels.
Set strict boundaries for your work hours. Communicate these to your team to protect your recovery time.

blocks.text: If you feel chronic stress or burnout symptoms, these tips are not a replacement for professional health support. Please reach out to a doctor or counselor if you need help.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps reduce your stress

Lazur acts as a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. It helps you get work done faster by reducing the need for constant manual input. Instead of clicking through menus, you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask a question. Lazur sees your screen and answers out loud. This keeps your eyes on the content instead of the interface. You can use it to draft emails in Gmail, search for info in Slack, or organize your calendar in Fantastical.
Practical ways to use Lazur for sales

items: Ask Lazur to explain a complex setting in Salesforce or your CRM.
Use dictation to draft quick responses to prospects without typing every word.
Ask where a specific button is in your email client to avoid digging through menus.
Let Lazur research a lead in the background while you focus on your next call.

blocks.text: Your daily routine for less stress

Start your day with a clear plan. Use your first 15 minutes to organize your priorities. Do not check email immediately. Use a tool like Todoist to list your top three goals. During the day, use voice commands to handle small tasks quickly. This prevents your to-do list from piling up.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you or points at things on your screen. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Is my data safe when I use voice commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only listens and looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. Your data is not stored or used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on a PC?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is currently built for macOS only.
